summary: Stage 1 + stage 2. Prediction and decision-making under src/cam_live/predict, wired onto the real CamLiveModel: five heads registered on the model, five LossProviders (world model incl. fast-prior and latent-consistency terms, ALPaCA-style fast prior, evaluator on signed verified outcomes, and adapter variants), the runtime Predictor (registered multi-horizon predictions, immediate fast-belief update, resolution, decision-relevant VOI), DecisionMaker (exact probabilities for five rules, self-proposed randomised experiments), LatentPlanner, BackboneProposer (100 % schema-valid proposals from Qwen3-4B on two tool sets), and debug-scale learning evidence in LabWorld with honest failures recorded.

It is NOT shown to be useful: the latent transition's measured error on held-out real LabWorld transitions stays above the no-skill level at debug scale (k=1: 1.44 after a short head-only fit, 1.80 untrained; 1.0 = predicting the mean), so the controller correctly never allows more than one step and imagined values carry little information. No comparison of decisions with and without planning was run.

SE-06.limitations: Decision-relevant VOI through the fast posterior works on the real model and is exactly zero for the unpredictable-but-irrelevant gauge (surprise is not value). NOT done / not shown: (1) the probe is not valued above the gauge; (2) VOI-aware selection did not beat greedy; (3) the learned downstream-usefulness estimator is registered on the model and has its signal vector, but no LossProvider trains it and it is not scored against realised downstream learning on the real model (stage 1, tensor level: it did not beat the computed VOI).

It does not form mechanistic explanations, and concluding an experiment (analyse / conclude) and revising strategy from it are left to the agent loop.

not_done: Nothing in cam_live.agent / runtime calls cam_live.predict yet (master integrates): Predictor, DecisionMaker, BackboneProposer, LatentPlanner and default_providers are ready and documented in docs/B/API.md.
Providers were run with predict.labdata.train (plain Adam), not under Workstream D's ContinualLearner; EvaluatorLoss.add_outcome must be called by whoever reconciles verified outcomes.
No training on the real Qwen3-4B configuration: only an initialisation-level pass (prediction, decision, fast update, one backward per timescale). All learning evidence is debug scale in LabWorld.
The learned downstream-usefulness estimator (heads.downstream) has no LossProvider and is not scored against realised downstream learning on the real model.
No LossProvider trains the candidate policy (that is the reward workstream's inner update); B only shows that the policy head depends on the belief and can be trained.
Exploration rules are not compared with each other on a task beyond greedy vs VOI-aware.

The Predictor's cache of decision-time features is in memory: after a restart, outcomes of earlier predictions resolve their records but no longer update the fast belief (no rebuild from the experience store).
Experiment lifecycle beyond registration and assignment (analyse / conclude / revise) is available in ExperimentRegistry but not driven by B.
Planner: no evidence that imagined values improve decisions; continuation policy is the (untrained) candidate policy.
Binary fast-layer combination is an approximation; categorical outcomes are head-only; real-valued readings cannot inform count posteriors (B-CR-10).
heads.scaler (per-metric location / scale of real-valued outcomes) is plain data, not a tensor: the checkpoint code must store heads.scaler.state() next to the weights.
Diagnostics are statistically, not bit-wise, reproducible: record ids come from uuid4 (contracts.new_id) and select the bootstrap resamples of the ensemble.
JSON-Schema support is a subset ($ref, if/then/else, patternProperties, dependent*, format unchecked).
Master-owned contracts unchanged: 11 change requests open in docs/change_requests/B.md.
scientific_failures: World model on NEW mechanisms (heads only, no adaptation) does not beat the action-independent baseline: held-out NLL 1.666 vs 1.645 (6 h) and 2.211 vs 2.163 (2 d); gain CIs {'hi': 0.0281, 'lo': -0.068, 'mean': -0.0199, 'n': 20.0, 'n_rows': 156.0} / {'hi': -0.005, 'lo': -0.0981, 'mean': -0.0515, 'n': 20.0, 'n_rows': 156.0}. At debug scale the core did not learn to read an unseen channel's rate from the features in its context.

Fast adaptation lowers predictive NLL after the first observation (gain {'hi': 0.1874, 'lo': 0.0515, 'mean': 0.1194, 'n': 38.0, 'n_rows': 318.0}) but NOT the absolute error of the predicted mean (gain {'hi': 0.1151, 'lo': -0.532, 'mean': -0.2084, 'n': 38.0, 'n_rows': 318.0}): the posterior mostly corrects the spread and the log-rate, the mean stays noisy.

Evaluator calibration, prospective, held-out lifetimes: Brier 0.250 untrained -> 0.240 trained (CI 0.215..0.266); predicting the base rate gives 0.240. brier_improved=True, beats_base_rate=False; calibration slope 254.16 (CI 122.43..385.90). The trained evaluator is a calibrated constant (mean forecast 0.581, base rate 0.600, ECE 0.019): it does not discriminate between lifetimes at debug scale. A first run that trained it on only 60 lifetimes was worse than the untrained constant (Brier 0.277 vs 0.250; docs/evidence/B/diagnostics_family_run1_evaluator_60_lifetimes.json): it memorised lifetimes. The reported run trains it on batches drawn from 400 lifetimes.

VOI of the probe is not higher than VOI of the noisy gauge. Fast-layer path: both exactly 0 (a real-valued reading cannot update the count posterior; posteriors are per kind). Slow path (imagined reading enters a copy of the context): probe {'hi': 0.0604, 'lo': 0.0061, 'mean': 0.0332, 'n': 20.0} vs gauge {'hi': 0.0644, 'lo': 0.0137, 'mean': 0.039, 'n': 20.0}, probe minus gauge {'hi': 0.011, 'lo': -0.0226, 'mean': -0.0058, 'n': 20.0} - the debug-scale core has not learned to use probe readings, and its sensitivity to the large gauge values shows up as spurious value. The slow path is therefore off by default (voi_slow_path=False) and was not used for selection.

The plain estimator E[max Q(updated)] - max Q(current) is biased upwards with the assumed-density count update (VOI of acting {'hi': 1.3072, 'lo': 0.0713, 'mean': 0.6893, 'n': 20.0} against {'hi': 0.0117, 'lo': 0.0011, 'mean': 0.0064, 'n': 20.0} for the Jensen-gap estimator E[max] - max E on the same samples). A run with the plain estimator made VOI-aware selection need MORE interventions than greedy (greedy minus VOI {'hi': -2.3258, 'lo': -7.3106, 'mean': -4.8182, 'n': 11.0}, 11 paired seeds; docs/evidence/B/diagnostics_value_of_information_plain_estimator.json); the Predictor now uses the Jensen gap.

VOI-aware selection does not reach the target with fewer interventions than greedy: greedy minus VOI = {'hi': 0.6848, 'lo': -4.0181, 'mean': -1.6667, 'n': 12.0} over 12 paired seeds that both reached the target (reached: greedy 1.00, VOI 1.00).

Action quality vs raw outcome: quality is much less luck-driven (Spearman with true luck 0.05 vs 0.52) but the raw outcome correlates better with the decision's true advantage (0.77 vs 0.35) in new worlds.

Latent transition on held-out real transitions is worse than predicting the mean belief (normalised error 1.44 at k=1 after a short fit; 1.68 batch NMSE at the end of family training): imagination never extends beyond one step and is not shown to help.
At random initialisation the policy's dependence on the belief is small in absolute terms (KL 5.9e-05 debug model, 7.4e-05 real configuration); 4.42 after imitating a history-dependent behaviour.

[stage 1, tensor level] The learned DownstreamValueEstimator did not beat an accurate computed VOI on held-out probes (Spearman 0.617 vs 0.671; learned_beats_reference=False). It only beat a deliberately mis-specified reference (-0.335). The computed VOI stays the reference.

[stage 1, tensor level] Poisson-GLM VOI with the assumed-density update over-estimates the realised gain in magnitude (computed [0.55, 0.137, 0.0] vs realised [0.376, 0.103, 0.0]); the ranking of probes is correct and the irrelevant probe is exactly 0. Bernoulli: computed [0.0339, 0.0063, 0.0] vs realised [0.0327, 0.0104, 0.0].
[stage 1, tensor level] After training, the evaluator is still mildly over-confident on held-out trajectories: calibration slope 0.69 (1.0 = calibrated), ECE 0.068 (from 0.477).

[stage 1, tensor level] A plain bootstrapped ensemble (prior_scale=0) did not reliably report higher epistemic uncertainty off-distribution (off/in ratio below 1 in 2 of 12 runs, minimum 0.61); randomised prior functions are therefore on by default (minimum ratio 2.57 over 12 runs).
